rules.text: Defects noted: Evidence of {E9_RW_DEFECTS} was noted to parts or all retaining walls. You should arrange for further investigation by an appropriately qualified person. Retaining walls are designed to support the considerable weight of the ground behind them. Where the retaining wall is in poor condition, it may no longer be performing its intended function effectively. Repairs or replacement can be costly, as any new retaining wall must be designed and constructed to adequately resist the retained ground. You should instruct an appropriately qualified structural specialist to inspect the wall without delay and provide recommendations for any necessary remedial works. Where the retaining wall is shared with, or forms a boundary with, a neighbouring property, responsibility for repair and maintenance may be shared or otherwise affected by legal rights and obligations. Before any work is undertaken, your legal adviser should investigate ownership, maintenance responsibilities and any associated rights or liabilities, and explain the implications to you.
pdf: Defects noted: Evidence of movement, bulging, instability, damage, other was noted to parts or all retaining walls.

rules.text: The inspection was limited to those parts that were safely accessible at the time of inspection. No opening up, testing or dismantling of concealed elements was undertaken. Comments relate only to the visible condition of the structures inspected. This section relates to external features not reported elsewhere within this report, including carports, porches, balconies, Juliet balconies, roof terraces, external staircases, retaining walls, communal areas, and other ancillary external structures. Only those elements that were readily visible and safely accessible at the time of inspection have been assessed.

General Maintenance: External ancillary structures should be inspected periodically as part of routine property maintenance. Rainwater disposal, structural stability, guarding, fixings, waterproofing and external finishes should be maintained to reduce the risk of deterioration and ensure continued safe use.
